items.title: 'It was fully ignored': This woman's medical emergency in Ontario jail reflects broader health-care crisis
items.description: More than a third of complaints filed by prisoners in Ontario jails this year were health-related, as medical staffing dropped by nearly 50 per cent and inmate populations kept rising, a CBC data analysis shows. One former inmate suffered a septic wound and a miscarriage while incarcerated.

items.title: 3 kids die from influenza A-related complications since start of December in Ontario
items.description: Three children in Ontario have died from influenza A-related complications since the start of December, health officials said Monday.

items.title: Ontario has no plans to sell off stored U.S. alcohol for charity, Ford says
items.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says his government has no plan to sell off a stockpile of American alcohol sitting in storage to benefit charities over the holiday season, for fear it could harm local producers.

items.title: Want to recall a Canadian politician? It's not easy — if it's even allowed where you live
items.description: Only two provinces allow for the recall of politicians. But with the bar set high for the process, most politicians targeted are likely not in any jeopardy. Here's a closer look at recall legislation in Canada, its history, arguments for and against, and the chances of a recall succeeding.

items.title: 1 dead after ‘fall of ground' incident at Saskatchewan potash mine
items.description: The Mosaic Company said a 'fall of ground incident,' which is a collapse of rock or earth in an underground mine, took place early Monday morning and fatally injured a worker.

items.title: Flu blamed in deaths of 3 children in Ottawa area this month
items.description: Three children between the ages of five and nine have died from complications of influenza this month, health officials in Ottawa and a neighbouring region said Monday.

items.title: Transforming Health Care in the DTES Through Culture and Connection
items.description: At Kílala Lelum, we walk alongside our relatives to provide culturally grounded health care, harm reduction and social support.

items.title: Canada’s grocery code of conduct is coming in 2026. What it means for you
items.description: The code of conduct is a document where the stakeholders in the grocery industry have agreed on a set of rules to govern the relationship between grocers and their suppliers.

items.title: Montreal police to 'increase vigilance' after mass shooting at Hanukkah event in Australia
items.description: Montreal police said they will increase their vigilance and visibility in areas where Jewish neighbourhood celebrations are taking place until the end of Hanukkah after a mass shooting in Australia.

items.title: Saskatoon woman demands better access to social supports for homeless community
items.description: A Good Samaritan is demanding change from all levels of government after a frozen Saskatoon night exposed the trouble in accessing social support for those in need.

items.title: BC’s Hospital Crowding Problem Isn’t Improving, Data Shows
items.description: In the seven most overcapacity facilities, one in six patients was cared for in an unfunded ‘surge bed’ last year. First in a series.

items.title: Linguistic experts urge Carney government to stop using British spellings
items.description: Promoters of Canadian English say the federal government is sending the wrong message to the world with its recent use of British spelling in official documents, including the 2025 federal budget.

items.title: Manitoba Justice Reports In-Custody Death
New citizenship rules now in effect for ‘Lost Canadians.' What to know
items.description: The new rules under Bill C-3 will now allow Canadian citizenship to be passed down to people born or adopted abroad beyond the first generation, under certain conditions.

items.title: Founder of Moose Jaw health centre suggests ‘ALS drug industry’ was behind CBC investigation of his business
items.description: The man behind the Moose Jaw health centre that has claimed “a 100 per cent success rate in stopping the progression and in restoring function of people with ALS” says a recent CBC story about his company is evidence that he is seen as “a direct threat to the ALS drug industry.”

items.title: Manitoba Maintains Fiscal Path Even as Climate Change and Trump's Tariffs Pose Challenges
Tariffs and the end of ‘de minimis' mean mailing gifts to U.S. is trickier
items.description: Canadians sending packages south of the border might have to factor in the tariffs imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump this year.

items.title: Toronto bike share probing loyalty program, seeking $41M in new funding
items.description: Bike Share Toronto is looking at introducing a loyalty program, among other revenue streams, in a bid to end years of operating at a financial loss.

items.title: One dead in collapse at K3 underground mine in Esterhazy, Sask., Mosaic says
items.description: According to a statement issued by the Mosaic Company, the incident happened at the K3 underground mine in Esterhazy, approximately 90 kilometres southeast of Yorkton, Sask.

items.title: Bed-building program gives back while teaching a trade
items.description: Oyate Tipi Cumini Yape, a Winnipeg-based furniture bank, has made 250 beds for people in need this year with help from volunteers, including teens who get to learn a new skill while helping others.

items.title: Renters consider leaving N.L. after no-fault eviction ‘upheaved’ their lives
items.description: After moving to St. John's, N.L. from Ontario, a couple built a comfortable life in a two-bedroom apartment with their cat. Two years later a no-fault eviction forced them to start over.

items.title: Ontario teen sets Guinness World record for stacking bottle caps using chopsticks
Toronto man outruns newly-opened light rail train by 18 minutes
items.description: A Toronto man challenged the newly-opened Finch Light-Rail Transit to a race — and he won.
